- [TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2023/05/30 (Tue) 15:35
- [USER] User asked about the evolution of German literature to reflect traditional narratives and modern social issues.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] German literature has evolved over time to reflect traditional narratives and modern social issues, particularly in the wake of the two World Wars, the Cold War, and the reunification of East and West Germany.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Key developments in German literature include:
  - [ASSISTANT_SAID] 1. Romanticism: Characterized by emotion, nature, and individualism; notable works include Johann Wolfgang von Goethe's "The Sorrows of Young Werther" and Friedrich Schiller's "Wallenstein."
  - [ASSISTANT_SAID] 2. Realism: Emerged in the mid-19th century, focusing on objective representation of the world; writers include Theodor Fontane, Gottfried Keller, and Wilhelm Raabe.
  - [ASSISTANT_SAID] 3. Modernism: Early 20th-century literature reflecting political and social turmoil; notable writers include Franz Kafka, Thomas Mann, and Bertolt Brecht.
  - [ASSISTANT_SAID] 4. Post-War Literature: Explored themes of guilt and identity after WWII; writers include Heinrich Böll, Günter Grass, and Christa Wolf.
  - [ASSISTANT_SAID] 5. Contemporary Literature: Engages with modern issues like migration and globalization; notable authors include Herta Müller, Daniel Kehlmann, and Jenny Erpenbeck.
- [USER] User expressed interest in the information provided and asked for recommendations of contemporary German authors.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Recommended contemporary German authors:
  - [ASSISTANT_SAID] 1. Jenny Erpenbeck - Notable works include "Go, Went, Gone" and "The End of Days."
  - [ASSISTANT_SAID] 2. Daniel Kehlmann - Notable work includes "Measuring the World."
  - [ASSISTANT_SAID] 3. Juli Zeh - Notable work includes "Corpus Delicti."
  - [ASSISTANT_SAID] 4. Terézia Mora - Notable work includes "The Tiger's Wife."
  - [ASSISTANT_SAID] 5. Saša Stanišić - Notable work includes "Before the Feast."
